clauses.reason: Terminated by express supersession or revocation. The order's one paragraph amends section 602 of Executive Order 10480 by adding subsection (d): (d)(1) gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the President's reporting functions on offsets, and (d)(2) authorizes the International Trade Commission to collect information for the first report's data base. Section 904(a) of Executive Order 12919, signed June 3, 1994, begins "(a) The following are superseded or revoked:" and item (9) reads "(9) Executive Order No. 12521 of June 24, 1985 (50 FR 26335)." Item (3) lists Executive Order 10480 and item (10) lists Executive Order 12649. Executive Order 12919 has no effective-date sentence, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03 (a reading, disclosed; it was filed June 6 and printed June 7, 1994). Later event, recorded before the end: Executive Order 12649, signed 1988-08-11, deletes the text of section 602(d)(2) and inserts a new (d)(2) that substitutes the Bureau of Economic Analysis of the Department of Commerce for the International Trade Commission and refers to the reports required by section 309; the original (d)(2) named the International Trade Commission and the data base for 'the first such report'. That amendment replaced a whole subsection, so the substance of (d)(2) changed (note for the human reviewer); under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 the clause continues, amended, until the parent ends, and the amendment is a later event, not an end.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register machine text of Executive Order 12521 (50 FR 26335, PDF pages 9-11 of the 1985-06-26 issue; sha256 c0ec068c...), rebuilt from OCR word positions, headed "Executive Order 12521 of June 24, 1985" and "Offsets in Military-Related Exports", signed June 24, 1985. This matches the census register row (1985-06-24, Offsets in Military-related exports). Text and inventory: one operative paragraph that amends section 602 of Executive Order 10480 by adding a new subsection (d); it has two commands, (d)(1) (Director of the Office of Management and Budget performs the President's reporting functions on offsets under section 309 of the Defense Production Act) and (d)(2) (the International Trade Commission is authorized under section 705 of that Act to collect information for the data base of the first report). The machine inventory holds the paragraph as one clause, and I confirm it as one clause because both commands sit in the one amendment and end together. Ending: Executive Order 12919 of June 3, 1994, section 904(a), supersedes or revokes Executive Order 12521 by number, together with Executive Order 10480 (the parent order amended) and Executive Order 12649 (the later amendment of (d)(2)). Executive Order 12919 has no effective-date sentence, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03 (a reading, disclosed; it was filed June 6 and printed June 7, 1994). No later current-law predicate is needed because the status is NO. Original grade: Federal Register machine text; no ruling on transcriptions is needed.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Executive Order 12649 (signed 1988-08-11) deletes the text of section 602(d)(2) of Executive Order 10480 and inserts a new (d)(2) that names the Bureau of Economic Analysis of the Department of Commerce instead of the International Trade Commission; it is a strike-and-insert amendment, so under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 the clause continues, amended, and the amendment is recorded as a later event with before-and-after wording; it does not name Executive Order 12521 and does not end subsection (d)(1). (2) The International Trade Commission authority in (d)(2) was to collect information for 'the first such report'; no held source shows when that report was prepared or submitted, so no performance-based end is claimed. (3) A search of the held corpus for the number 12521 found only Executive Orders 12649 and 12919 and the order's own texts, and the OFR disposition-note search (machine search) lists two hits, again 12649 and 12919. No instrument before 12919 revokes or supersedes the order.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command that stands apart from the amendment of section 602 of Executive Order 10480. Subsection (d)(1) (reporting functions on offsets to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget) and subsection (d)(2) (collection of information for the data base) are both inside that amendment and both lie within the superseded list in section 904(a); neither is preserved by Executive Order 12919.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12919 does not preserve Executive Order 12521. Its section 401(a) delegates the President's responsibilities and authority under section 309 of the Defense Production Act with respect to offsets to the Secretary of Commerce, and section 401(b) assigns the annual offset report to the Secretary, so the reporting function continued under a new command. Section 903 keeps previously issued orders, regulations and other actions in effect 'except as they are inconsistent with this order' and keeps valid anything done under earlier delegations; I read that as covering acts already done under Executive Order 12521, not the order itself, because section 904(a)(9) supersedes the order by name (disclosed as a reading).","scope_check":"One clause. Executive Order 12919 section 904(a)(9) supersedes or revokes Executive Order 12521 as a whole, naming it by number, date and Federal Register citation, without limitation; section 904(a)(3) and (10) supersede or revoke Executive Order 10480 and Executive Order 12649 in the same list, so the amended parent and the later amendment end with it. I read the Federal Register text of 904 through its end; the only qualification is section 904(d), which concerns inconsistent provisions of other orders and does not limit the list."}

savings.reason: The function of reporting on offsets under section 309 of the Defense Production Act continued under a separate command: section 401(a) of Executive Order 12919 delegates the responsibilities and authority conferred on the President with respect to offsets to the Secretary of Commerce, and section 401(b) has the Secretary prepare the annual report. Acts already done under Executive Order 12521, such as information already collected, are completed acts that section 903 leaves valid. Nothing in Executive Order 12919 preserves the order itself.
